+# Per-alphabet lookup tables, built on first use. Plain dicts are used

+    alphabet: bytes
+) -> Tuple[List[bytes], List[bytes]]:
+    # pairs[hi * base + lo] is the two character encoding of digits hi, lo;
+    # singles[d] is the one character encoding of digit d
+    tables = _encode_tables.get(alphabet)
+    if tables is None:
+        tables = (list(map(bytes, product(alphabet, repeat=2))),
+                  [alphabet[d:d + 1] for d in range(len(alphabet))])
+        _encode_tables[alphabet] = tables
+    return tables

actions.reason: Replace functools.lru_cache on the per-alphabet table builders with module-level dict caches and look the tables up inline in b58encode_int and b58decode_int. This removes the functools import (and the collections/reprlib/etc. modules it pulls in) at module import time and replaces a cached-function call per encode/decode with a dict lookup. The encode table also stores the single-character encodings as a list, so the inner loop indexes a list instead of slicing the alphabet. Table contents, keys (alphabet, autofix) and error behaviour are unchanged; equivalence harness reports identical output. Measured: encode_ir 0.909, decode_ir 0.949, check_ir 0.937 of parent.
